result:
I found 5 of the 40 rules that didn't match their docstrings and fixed them all in `pricebook.py`. After the fixes, all 40 rules match their docstrings in my check script.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 04 | Threshold used `qty > 100`, so exactly 100 units got no discount | `qty >= 100` |
| 13 | Docstring says 7%, code applied 8% | `* 7 // 100` |
| 22 | Docstring has a 30,000 won cap, code had no cap | Added `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 29 | Cap was applied to the price instead of the discount (`min(base, 10000) * 3 // 100`), breaking the shared module docstring rule | Take 3% of the price first, then cap the discount at 10,000 |
| 37 | Used `round()`, breaking the shared rule that discounts are rounded down (`// 100`) | `base * 2 // 100` |

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that reads each rule's percentage, minimum quantity and cap from its docstring and builds a reference calculation from those values and the shared rules (round discounts down, cap the discount not the price, discount starts at the minimum quantity). It compares each rule against that reference at quantities just below, at and above its threshold, and at large quantities. It also checks that negative inputs raise an error. Before the fixes, exactly these 5 rules failed; afterwards, all 40 pass.

The check script is in the session's scratchpad folder, not the project, as `scratchpad/check.py`.
